# nish/sync/ring

bounded lock-free queues of byte records in a shared region, for handing work between processes on different cores.

```ts
import {
  MpscRing,
  RING_EMPTY,
  RING_TOO_SMALL,
  SpscRing,
  attachMpscRing,
  attachSpscRing,
  initMpscRing,
  initSpscRing,
  mpscRingBytes,
  spscRingBytes,
} from "nish/sync/ring";
```

```ts
import { createRegion, unlinkRegion } from "nish/sync/shm"
import { initSpscRing, attachSpscRing, spscRingBytes } from "nish/sync/ring"

const region = createRegion("jobs", spscRingBytes(65536)).expect("region")
const ring = initSpscRing(region, 0, 65536, true)
ring.tryPush(job, 0, job.length) // false when full

// The other process, with the region opened by name:
const ring = attachSpscRing(region, 0).expect("ring")
const n = ring.popWait(buf, 0, 1000) // the record's length, or RING_EMPTY
```

<scalar-detail title="Two rings">

`SpscRing` has one producer and one consumer, and holds
records of any length up to its capacity back to back: a record costs its
length rounded up to 4, plus 4, and a record written with `reserve` may
leave padding at a lap's end (a skip marker, below). `MpscRing` takes any number of producers
and one consumer, in fixed slots of `slotBytes` each (Vyukov's bounded
queue: a producer claims a slot with a compare-exchange on the enqueue
position, and each slot's sequence number says whose turn it is). Neither
takes a lock, so a push or a pop in a busy ring is a handful of loads and
stores and no system call.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="A ring lives at base in a SharedRegion">

`initSpscRing` and
`initMpscRing` write its header there, which the process that creates the
region does once, before anyone attaches; `attachSpscRing` and
`attachMpscRing` read it in any other process (or the same one) and refuse
memory with no ring of that kind at `base`. `spscRingBytes` and
`mpscRingBytes` say how many bytes a ring takes from `base`, which is a
multiple of 64 so the header's counters each have a cache line. Several
rings may share a region at different bases.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="In place">

An `SpscRing` producer may write a record into the ring
itself instead of copying one in, and a consumer may read one there:

```ts
const w: u8[] = ring.reserve(n) // empty when there is no room now
copyBytes(w, 0, body, 0, k)     // any u8[] writer, within w.length
ring.commit(k)                  // publishes w[0, k) as one record
```

```ts
const r: readonly u8[] = ring.peek() // the next record, in the ring
if (r.length > 0) {
  use(r)
  ring.release()                // frees it for the producer
} else {
  ring.tryPop(buf, 0)           // none, or one peek cannot lend
}
```

</scalar-detail>

A window is a `SharedRegion.lend` window: the ring keeps one for its
producer and one for its consumer and re-points them on every call, so
neither path allocates or makes a system call. `commit`, `abandon` and
`release` give the window back, which empties it: a reference kept past
them indexes nothing (each index panics) until the next `reserve` or
`peek` re-points it, and then sees that call's record. A reserved record
is always contiguous: when the rest of the lap is too short, `commit`
writes a skip marker there (a length word of -1, "the rest of this lap is
padding") and the record starts at the next lap. Every pop steps over a
marker. A record `tryPush` wrapped across the end cannot be lent, so `peek`
answers an empty window for it and `tryPop` takes it, as it does for a
record of length 0. A reservation is at most `capacity / 2 - 4` bytes, so
a ring of 8 can never reserve (it panics) and one of 16 allows 4. The
reserved bytes are not zeroed: `commit` only what was written. A consumer
that polls `peek` on a doorbell ring has no wait call yet (`popWait` takes
records, not windows).

<scalar-detail title="The format keeps its magic">

A ring no producer `reserve`s into is
byte for byte what it was, and a consumer built before the marker that
meets one panics with "the ring is corrupt", never reads padding as a
record. Both ends of a ring are normally one build, so a new magic would
buy a clearer panic at the cost of every attach of an existing ring.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Who may call what is not checked">

An `SpscRing` with two producers, or
either ring with two consumers, loses or repeats records; it never reads or
writes outside its region, because every access is a checked `SharedRegion`
access, and a length a broken peer wrote that cannot be a record's panics.
An `MpscRing` producer that dies between claiming a slot and filling it
stalls the consumer at that slot for good: a supervisor that restarts
producers makes a fresh ring.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="The doorbell">

A ring made with `doorbell` true lets the consumer sleep
instead of spinning: `popWait` spins a little, then says it is sleeping in
the header and sleeps on Linux's futex, and a push rings it only when that
flag is set (one `SEQ_CST` store and load on each side, so neither can miss
the other). A busy ring makes no system calls; an idle one makes two per
record, the consumer's wait and the producer's wake. Without the doorbell a
push is a release store and `popWait` answers `SHM_UNSUPPORTED`, as it does
off Linux, where the consumer polls `tryPop`. `popWait` reads the monotonic
clock for its deadline, so a program that imports this module reaches the
`clock` capability as well as `ffi`.

</scalar-detail>

Private helpers share the importing program's flat symbol namespace
(`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e), which is why each one carries the module's name.

## initMpscRing

Writes an `MpscRing`'s header at `base` and answers the ring: `slots`
slots, a power of two from 2, of `slotBytes` each, a multiple of 8 from 8,
and `doorbell` for `popWait`. A ring already there is reset.

## MpscRing

Any number of producers, one consumer, records of at most `slotBytes`.
Make it with `initMpscRing` or `attachMpscRing`.

```ts
class MpscRing
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new MpscRing(region: SharedRegion, base: i32)` |  |
| `base: i32` | Its header's offset in the region. |
| `doorbell: boolean` | Whether a push rings the consumer's doorbell. |
| `head: i64` | The consumer's position: records ever popped (this object's, as the consumer). |
| `region: SharedRegion` | The region the ring lives in. |
| `slotBytes: i32` | Each slot's payload bytes, a multiple of 8. |
| `slots: i32` | Slots, a power of two. |
| `popBatch(dst: u8[], lens: i32[]): i32` | Moves up to `lens.length` records into `dst`, back to back from 0, while they fit, and sets `lens[i]` to each one's length: how many it moved. |
| `popWait(dst: u8[], off: i32, timeoutMs: i32): i32` | `SpscRing.popWait`, for this ring. |
| `tryPop(dst: u8[], off: i32): i32` | Moves the next record into `dst` from `off` and answers its length: `RING_EMPTY` when there is none, `RING_TOO_SMALL` (keeping it queued) when it is longer than `dst.length - off`. |
| `tryPush( src: readonly u8[], off: i32, len: i32, ): boolean` | Queues `src[off, off + len)` as one record: false when every slot is taken now. A record longer than a slot panics. |

## SpscRing

One producer, one consumer, records of any length. Make it with
`initSpscRing` or `attachSpscRing`; each object keeps its own copy of the
position it owns and a cache of the other side's, so a push reads the
consumer's counter only when the ring looks full, and a pop the producer's
only when it looks empty.

```ts
class SpscRing
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new SpscRing(region: SharedRegion, base: i32)` |  |
| `base: i32` | Its header's offset in the region. |
| `capacity: i32` | Data bytes, a power of two. |
| `doorbell: boolean` | Whether a push rings the consumer's doorbell. |
| `found: i64` | The position of the record `lengthAt` last read, past any skip marker. |
| `head: i64` | The consumer's position: bytes ever popped (this object's, as a consumer). |
| `peekedEnd: i64` | The position past the record `peek` lent, or -1 for none. |
| `region: SharedRegion` | The region the ring lives in. |
| `reserved: i32` | The open reservation's bytes, or -1 for none. |
| `reservedPad: i32` | The padding the open reservation skips at the tail. |
| `seenHead: i64` | The other side's position, as last loaded. |
| `seenTail: i64` |  |
| `tail: i64` | The producer's position: bytes ever pushed (this object's, as a producer). |
| `view: u8[] \| null` | `peek`'s window, likewise. |
| `wnd: u8[] \| null` | `reserve`'s window, re-pointed by each call; null until the first. |
| `abandon(): void` | Drops the open reservation, publishing nothing; panics without one. |
| `commit(len: i32): void` | Publishes the reserved window's first `len` bytes as one record, the store `tryPush` makes. The window is given back, so it is empty after. Panics without a reservation, for `len` outside `[0, n]`, or when a `push` moved the window out of the ring. |
| `peek(): readonly u8[]` | The next record, lent in place as the ring's own bytes, without copying or blocking; `release` frees it for the producer. Empty (length 0) when there is none, and also for a record peek cannot lend: one `tryPush` wrapped across the end of the ring, or one of length 0. On an empty answer nothing is lent, and `tryPop` takes the record if there is one. Panics while a record is lent. |
| `popBatch(dst: u8[], lens: i32[]): i32` | Moves up to `lens.length` records into `dst`, back to back from 0, while they fit, and sets `lens[i]` to each one's length: how many it moved. One load of the producer's position and one store of the consumer's, however many records it moves. Panics while `peek` has a record lent. |
| `popWait(dst: u8[], off: i32, timeoutMs: i32): i32` | `tryPop`, but on an empty ring it polls briefly and then sleeps until a push rings the doorbell, for at most `timeoutMs` in all (negative: no limit): `RING_EMPTY` only once that has passed. `SHM_UNSUPPORTED` for a ring without a doorbell, or off Linux, where the caller polls `tryPop`. Panics while `peek` has a record lent, from `tryPop`, so the message names `tryPop`. |
| `release(): void` | Frees the record `peek` lent, the store `tryPop` makes, and gives the window back, so it is empty after. Panics when no record is lent. |
| `reserve(n: i32): u8[]` | A window of `n` bytes of the ring's own memory to write a record into, contiguous, without blocking: empty (length 0) when the ring has no room for it now. Nothing is published until `commit`; `abandon` drops it. `n` is from 1 (a window of 0 could not be told from no room; `tryPush` takes an empty record) to `capacity / 2 - 4`, so an empty ring always has room for one; outside that, or while a reservation is open, it panics. A ring of 8 has no such `n` and always panics; one of 16 allows 4. The bytes are not zeroed: they hold whatever the ring last held there. |
| `tryPop(dst: u8[], off: i32): i32` | Moves the next record into `dst` from `off` and answers its length: `RING_EMPTY` when there is none, `RING_TOO_SMALL` (keeping it queued) when it is longer than `dst.length - off`. Panics while `peek` has a record lent. |
| `tryPush( src: readonly u8[], off: i32, len: i32, ): boolean` | Appends `src[off, off + len)` as one record: false when the ring has no room for it now. A record longer than the ring could ever hold panics, and so does a call while a reservation is open. |

## Constants

<scalar-card title="-1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`RING_EMPTY: i32`

`tryPop`, `popWait`: the ring is empty (or the wait ran out).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`RING_TOO_SMALL: i32`

`tryPop`, `popWait`: the next record is longer than the room after `off` in `dst`; it stays queued.
